data.name: Divangi
data.gender_notes: Divangi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Divangi is derived from the Sanskrit words 'diva' (divine) and 'gani' (knowledge). This name symbolizes the divine knowledge bestowed upon a child. The name Divangi carries the meaning “Divine Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Divangi usually hope their child will grow to embody divine knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Divangi was the name of a queen who ruled over the ancient Hindu kingdom of Kalinga during the 2nd century BCE. She is best known for her role in the Kalinga War, in which she was defeated by Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Empire. According to inscriptions, Ashoka showed great mercy to the conquered people, including the defeated queen Divangi.

Another reference to Divangi is found in the 12th century CE Jain text 'Kalpa Sutra'. In this text, Divangi is mentioned as a queen of the Vatsa kingdom who ruled during the late 5th century BCE. She is known for her devotion to the Jain religion and her patronage of Jain monks.
